cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: You Handle the Evidence
cards.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take this raffle cashbox and broken key to the treasurer. I'd rather you dealt with her questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tape it shut and leave it on her desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No unattended cash. Hand it to her and count it together. Write down the total before you discuss the lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll ask how you snapped the key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say I turned it and it broke. No theories about force. Wait for her receipt, please.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 explicitly hands off the cashbox and awkward questions. A3 corrects B2's unattended storage, and A5 coaches the account of the break while leaving B responsible for handover proof.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's desk plan produces A3's person-to-person count. B4's expected question about the snapped key produces A5's limited factual answer and receipt instruction.

relationship.evidence: B2 proposes an efficient delivery and B4 reasonably anticipates the recipient's question. A's corrective handling makes B do more work rather than simply calling B incompetent.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's question to extend delegated work from delivery and counting to presenting the break without speculation and collecting proof.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies cashbox, broken key and treasurer before the later question. A3 makes the monetary responsibility concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's no-theories-about-force line seeks a favorable account while sounding precise; the receipt request closes the actual handover task.

coach2.stated: A1 presents a cashbox and broken key; B2 proposes desk storage; A3 requires a joint count; B4 says A snapped the key.
coach2.inferred: A is uncomfortable explaining damage but treats B as needing supervision to handle it.
coach2.missing: No secret theft or cash discrepancy must be invented; the damaged key alone motivates the awkward follow-up.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate found; all physical evidence is introduced before the ending.
